newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli security chief met PLO's Arafat in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israeli security chief met PLO's Arafat in Gaza.

text.p: An Israeli security chief met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat early on Thursday to discuss what Israel says was an attempted shooting attack by PLO police officers on a Jewish settlement, Israeli security sources said.

The head of Israel's Shin Bet security service, Ami Ayalon, told Arafat in a secret meeting overnight in Gaza that senior PLO security officials sent the officers. He demanded that Arafat take quick action against them, the sources said.
Arafat's adviser, Nabil Abu Rdaineh, said he was checking the report.
Israel arrested three Palestinian police officers in the West Bank on Monday, alleging they were on their way to carry out a shooting attack on a Jewish settlement near Nablus.
Israeli leaders have described the incident as flagrant violation of Israel-PLO peace deals.
"The fact...that Palestinian police worked to carry out attacks is very very serious," Foreign Minister David Levy said on Thursday.
"It is certain that peace will not advance by pressure, threats, incitement or violence," he told reporters in Jerusalem.
The Palestinian governor of Nablus, Mahmoud al-Alloul, said this week Israeli allegations about PLO police plotting an attack on Jews were "absolutely untrue".

"We asked them to hand the police back over. We will investigate the incident and take measures not according to the Israeli investigation but rather according to the Palestinian investigation," he told Reuters on Wednesday.
Tension in the West Bank and Gaza Strip has soared since Israel launched construction at a Jewish settlement site in Arab East Jerusalem last March.
